hero.headline: Air Force B-52 bomber crashes at California base, killing 8 crew members
hero.body:
An Air Force B-52 bomber crashed at Edwards Air Force Base in California, killing all eight crew members on board. The crash occurred at the desert installation, which serves as a primary testing facility for Air Force aircraft. An investigation is underway to determine the cause of the accident.

The B-52 Stratofortress is a long-range strategic bomber that has been in service with the Air Force for decades. These aircraft typically carry crews of five, though some missions require additional personnel. The bomber that crashed was conducting operations at Edwards, located in the Mojave Desert north of Los Angeles.

Edwards Air Force Base has served as a critical testing and development site for military aviation since the 1940s. The facility is known for its vast dry lake beds that provide emergency landing surfaces and its role in experimental aircraft programs. The base regularly hosts flight tests of both new and existing military aircraft platforms.

The B-52 fleet remains a cornerstone of American strategic bomber capability despite the age of the airframes. The Air Force continues to operate and modernize these aircraft, with plans to keep them in service for years to come. Fatal crashes involving B-52s are uncommon given the aircraft's long operational history and extensive safety protocols.

Military aviation accidents trigger comprehensive investigations that examine mechanical systems, maintenance records, weather conditions, and crew actions. The Air Force will conduct a thorough review to identify any factors that contributed to the crash. The investigation process typically takes months to complete as officials analyze flight data, wreckage, and other evidence to establish a definitive cause.

The crash has drawn attention from multiple news organizations covering the incident. CNN, USA Today, NBC Los Angeles, and other outlets have reported on the fatal accident at the California base. The story reflects the continued importance of safety oversight in military aviation operations.

Edwards Air Force Base occupies a significant place in American military history and continues to play a vital role in aircraft development and testing. The facility's location in the Mojave Desert provides unique advantages for conducting flight tests and emergency operations. The vast landscape and specialized infrastructure make it ideal for evaluating military aircraft performance across various conditions.

The loss of eight crew members represents a significant tragedy for the Air Force and the families of those involved. The investigation into what caused the crash will be closely monitored by military officials and aviation experts seeking to understand the circumstances surrounding the accident. As with all military aviation incidents, the findings from this investigation may lead to changes in operational procedures or aircraft maintenance protocols.

cards.headline: U.S. and Iran set to sign preliminary peace deal as negotiations continue
cards.teaser: The United States and Iran plan to sign a preliminary agreement Friday to end their military conflict, with both sides preparing for immediate follow-up negotia.
cards.body:
The United States and Iran plan to sign a preliminary agreement Friday to end their military conflict, with both sides preparing for immediate follow-up negotiations. Iran's foreign minister said new talks would begin right after the signing, while President Trump expressed hope the conflict would soon be resolved.

The deal requires Israeli forces to withdraw from Lebanon, according to statements from Iranian officials. Trump separately commented on Israel's military operations against Hezbollah in Lebanon, saying he was not satisfied with how Israel had conducted its campaign and suggesting Syria should take on that role instead. The connection between the U.S.-Iran negotiations and Israeli military presence in Lebanon has emerged as a key component of the diplomatic framework.

Trump made remarks about the negotiations while attending the G7 summit, where he stated the war in Ukraine has no impact on the United States. The mood at the summit appeared lighter than expected following news of the U.S.-Iran preliminary deal, though Trump's comments highlighted continuing disagreements among allied nations. His history at G7 gatherings has been marked by strained relationships and behavior that challenges traditional diplomatic protocol.

For Iranians, the deal represents less a victory than a necessity, according to reports from Tehran. Many citizens are focused on whether the agreement will reduce prices and lower the threat of future military action rather than celebrating it as a political triumph. The Iranian government has framed the deal as a success, but public sentiment reflects war fatigue and economic concerns.

The conflict's impact has extended beyond the immediate region. At a World Cup match in Los Angeles, Iran's national team drew spectators who came not to watch soccer but to protest the government in Tehran, illustrating the political divisions the war has deepened. The preliminary agreement marks a potential turning point, though both sides acknowledge substantial negotiations remain before a final resolution.

cards.headline: Senate Republicans seek text of Iran agreement
cards.teaser: Senate Majority Leader John Thune says Republican leaders are pressing the Trump administration for the text of a memorandum of understanding with Iran but have not yet seen it.
cards.body:
Senate Majority Leader John Thune said Tuesday that Republican leaders are demanding to see the text of a memorandum of understanding that would end the military conflict with Iran, but have not yet received a briefing on the agreement.

"We're trying to get it," Thune told reporters at the Capitol, acknowledging that even senior lawmakers lack basic information about the preliminary accord announced Sunday.

The memorandum centers on reopening the Strait of Hormuz and lifting the United States' naval blockade in the region. It also includes potential financial incentives for Iran if the country meets certain conditions. Vice President JD Vance described the MOU as "a very general document" about a page long, with specifics to be determined during further negotiations.

Republican senators returning to Washington expressed widespread skepticism about the agreement. Thune said his primary concerns involve compliance and enforcement mechanisms. "I think the issues are going to be compliance, and how are you going to enforce that," he said, adding that the deal would be favorable if financial incentives are tied to Iran eliminating its enriched uranium and abandoning its nuclear program.

Senator Thom Tillis of North Carolina questioned the secrecy surrounding the agreement. "If it's a secret deal then how can I take it seriously?" he asked.

Other Republicans also sought clarity before the deal moves forward. The memorandum reportedly includes the possibility of releasing Iran's frozen funds, sanctions relief, and a 300 billion dollar reconstruction fund contingent on Tehran meeting specific benchmarks. Vance indicated that Gulf states would finance the reconstruction fund, not the United States.

Vance said the White House would release the text this week, emphasizing that "Iran doesn't get a dime of money unless they perform their obligations." However, the administration has not yet addressed key questions about verification of Iran's nuclear compliance or who will oversee the destruction of enriched uranium stored at damaged nuclear sites.

The agreement marks President Trump's second approach to Iran policy. He withdrew from the 2015 nuclear accord during his first term, a deal that allowed Iran to reclaim frozen assets. Trump has repeatedly criticized that agreement as sending "pallets of cash" to Iran.

Senator Lindsey Graham, a Trump ally and longtime Iran hawk, called for Congress to review and vote on the final agreement. "Let's look at it and see what it actually is," Graham said, expressing doubt about Iranian claims regarding the deal's benefits.

Vance responded by cautioning Graham and others against believing "hardliner propaganda in Iran" rather than focusing on the actual agreement terms.

cards.headline: FBI disrupts alleged plot targeting White House UFC event
cards.teaser: Federal agents arrested multiple suspects accused of planning an attack on a UFC event, with investigators saying the plotters wanted to start a revolution.
cards.body:
The FBI has arrested multiple suspects in connection with an alleged plot to attack a UFC event held at the White House. According to newly unsealed court documents, the suspects planned to use drones as part of the attack. FBI Director Kash Patel confirmed that law enforcement disrupted the planned attacks before they could occur.

The UFC event took place at the White House over the past weekend. Several people remain in custody following the investigation. Additional details are expected to be released once charges are unsealed in the case.

cards.headline: Plane carrying skydivers crashes in Missouri, killing 12
cards.teaser: A small aircraft carrying experienced skydivers plummeted to the ground in Butler, Missouri, killing everyone on board.
cards.body:
Twelve people died when a plane carrying skydivers crashed in Butler, Missouri. The aircraft went down during what was described as favorable conditions for skydiving operations. Some of the skydivers killed in the crash were experienced jumpers, according to reports.

Skydive KC, the operation involved in the incident, released a statement following the crash. Among the victims was an orchestra teacher from Oak Park High School. The crash occurred at a skydiving facility that regularly conducts jump operations in the area.

cards.headline: Oil Prices Fall Below $80 Per Barrel as Traders Assess U.S.-Iran Deal
cards.teaser: Brent crude oil dipped below $80 per barrel for the first time since March as markets reacted to prospects of restored energy flows.
cards.body:
Oil prices are falling as markets react to a U.S.-Iran deal framework that will reopen the Strait of Hormuz waterway. Brent crude has dipped below $80 per barrel for the first time since March, reflecting trader optimism about normalized shipping operations and eased supply concerns.

Stock markets have shown mixed performance following the previous day's strong rallies. The energy market shift comes as investors assess the economic implications of restored Iranian oil production and export capacity.

cards.headline: Trump says Russia should make peace deal with Ukraine
cards.teaser: President Trump said Russia should make a deal with Ukraine to end the four-year invasion, noting both countries have lost tremendous numbers of people.
cards.body:
At the Group of Seven summit in France, President Trump urged Russia to negotiate an end to its four-year invasion of Ukraine. Trump emphasized that both Russia and Ukraine have suffered significant losses in the conflict.

Trump's remarks came as G7 allies worked to keep Ukraine on the agenda amid discussions about Middle East tensions. The president has previously expressed interest in negotiating a resolution to the war.

hero.headline: Trump says Ukraine war has no impact on U.S. at G7 summit
hero.teaser: President Trump told allied leaders at the G7 gathering that the war in Ukraine does not affect the United States.
hero.body:
Trump's comments at the G7 summit highlighted ongoing divisions among allied nations over priorities and global security concerns. The mood at the meeting appeared lighter than anticipated following news of the preliminary U.S.-Iran deal.

Trump has a history of creating tension at G7 summits through his behavior and statements, which have often challenged the traditional diplomatic decorum of the annual gatherings. His presence at these meetings has consistently tested relationships with other world leaders.

cards.headline: Venezuela signs infrastructure deal with General Electric
cards.teaser: Venezuela's interim government reached an agreement with the U.S. energy company to rebuild the country's power grid.
cards.body:
Venezuela's interim government has partnered with General Electric to rebuild the country's power grid. The agreement represents growing cooperation between U.S. companies and Venezuela's leadership on infrastructure projects.

The deal underscores a shift in economic engagement between the two nations, with American firms increasingly involved in Venezuela's energy sector initiatives.

cards.headline: U.K. government announces social media ban for children under 16
cards.teaser: British officials unveiled plans to prohibit social media access for anyone under age 16.
cards.body:
The UK government has announced a ban on social media access for all children under 16. Prime Minister Keir Starmer framed the move as "giving children their childhood back." The ban would cover major platforms including Snapchat, TikTok, YouTube, Instagram, Facebook, and X.

The announcement aligns with similar restrictions being pursued in Australia and other countries. The father of a murdered teenager has publicly supported the ban, citing online safety concerns. Social media companies have opposed the proposed restrictions, while questions persist about enforcement mechanisms and whether educational or communication exceptions would apply.

cards.headline: Trump and Modi to meet as U.S.-India relations face setbacks
cards.teaser: The two leaders will hold talks despite a series of problems in bilateral relations since they last met over a year ago.
cards.body:
Relations between the United States and India have experienced multiple setbacks in recent months, creating challenges for the traditionally friendly partnership. The meeting will test whether personal rapport between Trump and Modi can help reset diplomatic ties.

Both leaders have publicly praised each other in the past, but policy disagreements and diplomatic friction have complicated the relationship. The outcome of the meeting could determine the direction of U.S.-India cooperation on trade, security, and regional issues.

cards.headline: Iran's World Cup team draws protesters in Los Angeles
cards.teaser: The Iranian national soccer team's first match attracted spectators who came to demonstrate against the government in Tehran rather than watch the game.
cards.body:
Iranian-Americans gathered outside the Iran versus New Zealand match at the World Cup in Los Angeles to protest against Tehran's clerical regime. The demonstrations reflected broader political divisions within the Iranian diaspora community.

The high-profile sporting event became a platform for expressing grievances against Iran's government, as protesters used the international tournament to amplify their message opposing the regime.

cards.headline: FBI stops alleged plot targeting White House UFC event
cards.teaser: Multiple suspects are in custody after federal agents disrupted a plan that would have used drones, according to FBI director Kash Patel.
cards.body:
Law enforcement disrupted a planned attack on a UFC event held at the White House, according to FBI Director Kash Patel. Multiple suspects were taken into custody as a result of the investigation.

Newly unsealed court documents reveal that the alleged plot involved the use of drones. The threat was identified and stopped before the event took place.

cards.headline: Motor oil costs rise amid Iran war supply disruptions
cards.teaser: The cost of motor oil and lubricants is climbing as the conflict with Iran disrupts global supply chains, a problem that persists despite diplomatic progress.
cards.body:
Americans are paying more for oil changes as motor oil and lubricant prices surge. Though the U.S. is the world's largest crude oil producer, it doesn't lead in motor oil production. The war with Iran has disrupted supply chains for lubricants, driving costs higher.

A tentative diplomatic deal to end the conflict won't immediately resolve the pricing problem. The motor oil market relies on international supply networks strained by the war, affecting routine vehicle maintenance costs nationwide.

cards.headline: Algae bloom turns renovated reflecting pool green after $14.2 million project
cards.teaser: Green algae has appeared in the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool after a costly renovation aimed at turning the water blue as part of an American flag design.
cards.body:
The Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool has turned green with algae following a $14.2 million renovation project. The administration had promised the work would eliminate algae problems and transform the pool into a striking "American flag blue" centerpiece at the historic monument.

The algae bloom has returned despite the costly renovation, proliferating amid warm weather conditions. The green water undermines the intended visual effect of the recent project.

cards.headline: World Cup visitors discover American food chains and free refills
cards.teaser: International visitors attending the World Cup in the United States are experiencing American dining culture, from regional chains to unlimited soft drinks.
cards.body:
International visitors to the World Cup are discovering American food culture beyond the soccer matches. Tourists are exploring regional chains including Buc-ee's, Waffle House, and Wawa, with the concept of free soda refills capturing particular attention from those unfamiliar with the practice.

These culinary experiences are becoming a notable part of the World Cup visit for many international fans. American dining establishments and their customs are drawing interest alongside the tournament itself, leaving an impression on visitors from countries where such offerings differ significantly.

cards.headline: Kennedy Center name change covered by tarp as legal dispute continues
cards.teaser: The Kennedy Center has removed a name from its exterior, but the change remains hidden under a tarp as legal proceedings continue.
cards.body:
Trump's name is being removed from the Kennedy Center's facade under court order, but a large blue and white tarp currently conceals the work. The removal process is ongoing as the performing arts center complies with the legal requirement to take down the signage.

The covered nameplate has drawn attention to the symbolic nature of the removal itself. The Kennedy Center is managing the physical alterations to its building while the legal situation surrounding the name change continues to develop.

hero.headline: SpaceX Acquires AI Start-Up Cursor for $60 Billion in All-Stock Deal
hero.body:
SpaceX has agreed to purchase Cursor, an AI coding company, in an all-stock transaction valued at $60 billion. The acquisition occurred just days after SpaceX completed its historic initial public offering, marking a significant expansion of Elon Musk's artificial intelligence portfolio.

The deal was completed through an option that SpaceX had previously arranged with Cursor, suggesting the two companies had negotiated terms before the start-up's public debut. Under the all-stock structure, Cursor shareholders will receive SpaceX shares rather than cash compensation, directly linking their financial interests to the aerospace company's future performance.

SpaceX's stock price surged following the acquisition announcement. The company's shares climbed 14 percent, pushing its overall market value beyond $2.9 trillion. This stock performance allowed SpaceX to surpass Amazon and become the world's fifth-most valuable company. The strong trading activity reflected continued investor enthusiasm following the company's record-breaking IPO, which valued SpaceX at approximately $2.1 trillion on its opening day.

SpaceX's initial public offering represented a historic moment for the company. Trading began at $150 per share, well above the pre-opening price of $135, and reached a high of $176 during the day's session. By market close, shares had settled at $160, representing a 19 percent increase from the opening price.

The acquisition strengthens SpaceX's capabilities in artificial intelligence technology. The company told IPO investors that it identified a $26 trillion addressable market in AI. Access to Cursor's coding technology could support SpaceX's operations across multiple divisions, including rocket development and its Starlink satellite internet services.

Musk's personal wealth has grown substantially from these developments. According to the Bloomberg rich list, his net worth now stands at approximately $1.11 trillion, making him the world's wealthiest individual. The combination of SpaceX's successful public market debut and the major acquisition represents a significant period for the company and Musk's broader business interests.

The Cursor acquisition signals SpaceX's commitment to competing directly in the artificial intelligence sector, an area where major technology companies have substantially increased their investments. This move complements Musk's existing AI ventures and could accelerate development of autonomous systems and software tools integrated throughout SpaceX's operations.

SpaceX operates as a conglomeration of several Musk-led businesses, including the Starlink satellite and internet provider, the xAI artificial intelligence company, the X social media platform, and the core SpaceX rocket business. The company generated $18.7 billion in revenue during the previous year, though it recorded an operating loss of $4.3 billion, reflecting its significant ongoing investment in research and development across its various divisions.

cards.headline: Oil Prices Fall Below $80 Per Barrel as Traders Assess U.S.-Iran Deal
cards.teaser: Brent crude oil dipped below $80 per barrel for the first time since March as markets reacted to prospects of restored energy flows.
cards.body:
Oil prices are falling as markets react to a U.S.-Iran deal framework that will reopen the Strait of Hormuz waterway. Brent crude has dipped below $80 per barrel for the first time since March, reflecting trader optimism about normalized shipping operations and eased supply concerns.

Stock markets have shown mixed performance following the previous day's strong rallies. The energy market shift comes as investors assess the economic implications of restored Iranian oil production and export capacity.

cards.headline: Yum Brands Sells Pizza Hut for $2.7 Billion to Sharpen Focus on Taco Bell and KFC
cards.teaser: The restaurant company is selling Pizza Hut in two separate deals as the chain's sales have lagged with the rise of delivery culture.
cards.body:
Yum Brands has agreed to sell Pizza Hut for $2.7 billion in two separate transactions, exiting the struggling pizza chain to focus on its stronger Taco Bell and KFC brands. Private equity firm LongRange Capital and Yum China will acquire the business, which has seen sales lag as delivery culture has changed the restaurant landscape.

Pizza Hut's performance has declined relative to Yum Brands' other chains, prompting the decision to divest. The sale allows Yum to concentrate resources on Taco Bell and KFC, where the company sees stronger growth prospects. The two-part deal structure splits the business between domestic and international operations.

cards.headline: Binance Set to Lose EU License Bid and Permission to Operate in the Bloc
cards.teaser: The world's largest cryptocurrency exchange is preparing for a potential exit from the European Union as its regulatory application faces rejection.
cards.body:
Binance is set to lose its bid for a license to operate in the European Union, with sources indicating the exchange will be denied permission to offer services in the bloc. The decision would force the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange to exit EU markets, marking a significant regulatory setback for the company.

Binance has stated its European regulatory application is compliant despite reports of rejection by Greek authorities. The exchange has reaffirmed its commitment to European users and compliance as the MiCA regulatory deadline approaches. The company is preparing contingency plans as its local license application remains in limbo.

cards.headline: Fertilizer Prices Rise as Iran War Affects American Farmers
cards.teaser: The conflict and lower crop prices have hurt makers of sulfur-based supplements, though farmers continue buying nitrogen-based products.
cards.body:
American farmers face rising fertilizer costs as the Iran war disrupts supply chains and affects agricultural input prices. Makers of sulfur-based supplements have been particularly hurt by the combination of war-related disruptions and lower crop prices, which squeeze profit margins for agricultural producers.

Farmers are expected to continue purchasing nitrogen-based fertilizers regardless of cost increases, as these products are essential for crop production. The price pressures add to existing challenges in the agricultural sector, where producers must balance rising input costs against uncertain commodity prices in global markets.

cards.headline: Iran War Has Permanently Altered Global Economy
cards.teaser: The conflict between the U.S., Israel, and Iran has reshaped the global economic order in ways unlikely to reverse.
cards.body:
The war involving the United States, Israel, and Iran has permanently altered the global economy, with effects that will persist beyond the conflict itself. Economies are unlikely to simply return to pre-war patterns after the bombing campaign, according to analysts assessing the long-term structural changes.

The global order has been reshaped by the conflict, with implications for trade routes, energy markets, and international commerce. The changes reflect shifts in geopolitical relationships and economic dependencies that emerged during the war, creating a new baseline for international business operations.

cards.headline: Working Parents Report Insufficient Time for Children and Personal Pursuits
cards.teaser: A Pew survey shows most working parents like having jobs but say work leaves too few hours for family and other activities.
cards.body:
Working parents say they are in a losing battle over their time, with most reporting that employment leaves insufficient hours for their children and personal pursuits, according to a new Pew Research Center survey. While the majority of working parents express satisfaction with having jobs, they cite time constraints as a persistent challenge in balancing professional and family responsibilities.

The survey findings highlight ongoing tensions between work demands and family life in American households. Parents across income levels and employment types reported feeling squeezed for time, suggesting the issue transcends specific job categories or economic circumstances.

hero.headline: India bans Telegram through June 22 over exam fraud
hero.teaser: The Indian government has ordered a temporary nationwide ban on Telegram and required the messaging app to disable its message editing feature.
hero.body:
India has imposed restrictions on Telegram that include a nationwide ban on the messaging application until June 22. The government cited concerns about exam fraud as the basis for the action.

Authorities also required Telegram to disable the app's message editing feature as part of the restrictions. The temporary ban affects all users within India during the specified period.

cards.headline: SpaceX valuation reaches $2.7 trillion days after public debut
cards.teaser: SpaceX's market valuation has climbed to $2.7 trillion since shares began trading on Friday, representing a $1 trillion increase in just days.
cards.body:
SpaceX's market valuation has surged to $2.7 trillion since its Friday debut on the Nasdaq, making it the world's fifth most valuable company and surpassing Amazon. The $1 trillion jump in just days reflects strong investor demand for the aerospace company's shares.

The IPO milestone also boosted Elon Musk's personal wealth to $1.11 trillion, making him the world's first trillionaire according to the Bloomberg rich list. Days after going public, SpaceX agreed to acquire AI coding startup Cursor for $60 billion, signaling aggressive expansion plans in its new public phase.

cards.headline: Flutterwave reaches $3.2 billion valuation with Ripple investment
cards.teaser: African payments company Flutterwave has secured funding from blockchain company Ripple, reaching a new $3.2 billion valuation.
cards.body:
Flutterwave, an African payments infrastructure company, has achieved a $3.2 billion valuation. Blockchain company Ripple participated in the funding round as both an investor and strategic partner.

The fintech startup provides payment infrastructure solutions across Africa. Ripple's dual role as investor and partner marks a significant collaboration between the payments platform and the blockchain firm.

cards.headline: Justice Department defends xAI gas turbines as security matter
cards.teaser: The Department of Justice has stated that xAI must continue operating unpermitted gas turbines, citing national, economic, and energy security concerns.
cards.body:
The Justice Department has claimed that xAI's use of unpermitted gas turbines serves national, economic, and energy security interests. The statement comes amid regulatory questions about the turbines' operation without proper permits.

According to the Justice Department, the Pentagon requires xAI to maintain use of the gas turbines. The department framed the continued operation as necessary for security purposes despite the lack of permits.

cards.headline: Plaud reports $100 million software revenue after selling 2 million AI notetakers
cards.teaser: AI notetaker company Plaud has surpassed $100 million in annual recurring revenue after shipping more than 2 million devices.
cards.body:
Plaud has reached over $100 million in annual recurring revenue from its software business, the company reported. The milestone follows shipments of more than 2 million AI-powered notetaking devices.

The company competes in a market with numerous AI-powered meeting and note-taking products. Plaud offers hardware devices designed to record and transcribe conversations using artificial intelligence.

cards.headline: Robinhood cuts 10 percent of workforce without citing AI
cards.teaser: Robinhood CEO Vlad Tenev announced layoffs affecting 10 percent of employees, notably omitting any mention of artificial intelligence in his statement.
cards.body:
Robinhood has reduced its workforce by 10 percent, CEO Vlad Tenev announced. The layoffs affect thousands of employees at the financial services company.

Tenev's announcement notably did not reference artificial intelligence as a reason for the cuts. This stands in contrast to many other tech industry executives who have recently attributed job reductions to the need to restructure and capitalize on AI capabilities.

cards.headline: Mobileye to launch robotaxi service in US city in 2027
cards.teaser: The autonomous driving technology company will enter the US robotaxi market with a standalone service using its Moovit platform.
cards.body:
Mobileye will launch a robotaxi service in a US city in 2027, the company announced. The service represents Mobileye's entry into the American autonomous taxi market.

The robotaxi operation will use Mobileye's Moovit platform as its foundation. The company has not disclosed which US city will host the initial launch of the service.

hero.headline: Venus and Serena Williams to play doubles at Wimbledon
hero.body:
Venus and Serena Williams will compete together in the women's doubles draw at Wimbledon after receiving a wildcard entry to the tournament. The All England Club announced the decision as part of its wildcard selections, with organizers noting this was one of the most anticipated announcements in recent memory due to Serena's comeback after four years away from professional tennis.

The sisters have not played doubles together since the 2022 US Open, where they lost in the opening round. This Wimbledon partnership marks a significant return for both players, who have achieved considerable success at the venue throughout their careers, including six women's doubles titles at the tournament.

Serena, a seven-time singles champion, did not request a singles wildcard for Wimbledon and has remained unclear about whether she intends to pursue singles competition. At 44 years old, she returned to competition recently at Queen's Club, where she won her opening match in doubles with Victoria Mboko. Venus, a five-time singles champion, also did not receive a singles wildcard. The 46-year-old has remained active on the professional tour since her 1994 debut, pausing only due to health-related issues.

The Williams sisters are among the most successful doubles pairings in tennis history. Together, they have won 14 Grand Slam doubles titles, ranking as the joint-second highest total in the open era. They have claimed six women's doubles titles specifically at Wimbledon, the highest number in the open era, and have earned three Olympic gold medals in women's doubles competition.

The wildcard system at Wimbledon allows the All England Club to grant tournament entry to players who may lack sufficient ranking points for automatic qualification but bring significant interest to the event. This approach enables the organizers to include notable competitors who might otherwise miss the draw.

Wimbledon organizers made several other notable wildcard selections. Maja Chwalinska, who reached the French Open women's singles final as a qualifier, received a wildcard and will hold the unusual dual status of both wildcard and seeded player at a Grand Slam tournament due to her recent ranking jump to number 21. Veteran players Stan Wawrinka and Grigor Dimitrov also received singles wildcards, while Britain's Dan Evans and Henry Searle earned a doubles wildcard together.

The announcement reflected the high level of attention surrounding Serena's return to professional tennis. Before Wimbledon, she competed in doubles at the Berlin WTA tournament alongside Karolina Muchova, the number 10 singles player. The Williams sisters' participation in the doubles draw adds considerable attention to Wimbledon's doubles competition, which typically receives less focus than the singles events at major tournaments.

cards.headline: Texas Tech quarterback Brendan Sorsby to enter NFL supplemental draft
cards.teaser: Quarterback Brendan Sorsby plans to apply for the NFL's supplemental draft amid ongoing legal disputes over his NCAA eligibility.
cards.body:
Texas Tech quarterback Brendan Sorsby is entering the NFL's supplemental draft after his college eligibility became disputed. The move comes amid legal challenges from the Big 12 and NCAA over betting violations he admitted to during his college career. Sorsby had until June 22 to decide whether to pursue the supplemental draft option.

The supplemental draft allows players with eligibility issues or other complications to enter the NFL outside the regular draft cycle. Teams bid for selection rights, with draft position determining the order. For Sorsby, the supplemental route may resolve the ongoing eligibility disputes while allowing NFL teams to evaluate him despite his gambling violations.

cards.headline: Raiders players share early impressions of rookie quarterback Fernando
cards.teaser: Coaches and players discussed their initial reactions to the Raiders' first overall pick during organized team activities.
cards.body:
The Las Vegas Raiders gathered feedback from coaches and players about their first impressions of rookie quarterback Fernando during organized team activities. Fernando was selected first overall in the most recent NFL draft.

The early assessments provide insight into how the rookie is adjusting to professional football and building relationships with his new teammates during the offseason program.

cards.headline: NFL executives name their favorite offseason moves
cards.teaser: League sources identified their top transactions from the offseason, ranging from major contracts to unexpected draft selections.
cards.body:
NFL executives shared their top offseason moves in conversations with league sources. The selections ranged from major free agent signings and trades to standout draft picks.

These moves reflect which teams league insiders believe made the most significant improvements during the offseason. The transactions executives highlighted represent different strategic approaches that they view as particularly impactful or well-executed.

cards.headline: Aldon Smith's family to have brain examined for CTE
cards.teaser: The family of former NFL defensive lineman Aldon Smith will send his brain to Boston for examination to determine if CTE contributed to his death.
cards.body:
Aldon Smith's family has decided to send his brain to medical experts in Boston to determine whether chronic traumatic encephalopathy contributed to his death. The former NFL defensive lineman's brain will be examined by specialists who study the degenerative condition.

CTE is linked to repeated head trauma and has been identified in many former football players. A definitive diagnosis of the disease can only be made through post-mortem brain examination.

cards.headline: Rory McIlroy criticizes proposed PGA Tour format changes
cards.teaser: The golfer expressed concern that new Track Two events could become second-tier competitions under the tour's updated format plans.
cards.body:
Rory McIlroy has expressed concern about the PGA Tour's proposed format updates, particularly the "Track Two" events being created as part of the restructuring. He worries these new events could become "glorified Korn Ferry events," referencing the tour's developmental circuit.

McIlroy's comments suggest skepticism about whether the reformatted tour will preserve the competitive quality and prestige associated with traditional PGA Tour events.

cards.headline: Brooks Koepka plans to play U.S. Open after hand injury
cards.teaser: The golfer confirmed he will compete in this week's U.S. Open after withdrawing from last week's Canadian tournament.
cards.body:
Brooks Koepka plans to play in this week's U.S. Open after pulling out of last week's RBC Canadian Open due to a hand injury. Koepka confirmed he will compete in the major championship, stating "I'm gonna go."

His withdrawal from Canada had raised questions about whether he would be available for the U.S. Open. His decision to play means he will compete despite the recent injury concern.

hero.headline: Guillermo del Toro Warns of Cinema Illiteracy as AI Reshapes Film Industry
hero.body:
Director Guillermo del Toro has issued a stark warning about the future of filmmaking, stating that the industry stands on the verge of cinema illiteracy as artificial intelligence and business consolidation transform the creative landscape. The Oscar-winning filmmaker made the comments while discussing threats to creative freedom in contemporary cinema.

Del Toro expressed deep concern about what he sees as fundamental changes to how audiences understand and engage with visual storytelling. His warning comes at a time when AI tools are increasingly being adopted across the entertainment industry for tasks ranging from visual effects to script development. The director framed the issue as both a technological and cultural crisis that could fundamentally alter the relationship between filmmakers and their audiences.

The filmmaker's concerns extend beyond technology to include the broader forces reshaping Hollywood. Business consolidation has accelerated in recent years, with major studios merging and streaming platforms restructuring their content strategies. Del Toro suggested these corporate changes compound the challenges posed by AI, creating multiple simultaneous pressures on creative freedom.

Del Toro has built a career on distinctive visual storytelling, from Pan's Labyrinth to The Shape of Water, which won the Academy Award for Best Picture in 2018. His approach emphasizes practical effects and carefully crafted imagery, a methodology that stands in contrast to the automated processes AI promises to deliver. The director's perspective carries particular weight given his decades of experience navigating the intersection of artistic vision and commercial filmmaking.

Currently in the UK to receive a BFI fellowship, an honor he described as especially meaningful given the influence of British cinema on his work, del Toro continues to champion traditional filmmaking approaches. His recent 2025 adaptation of Frankenstein reflects his commitment to crafting nuanced, thoughtful cinema that explores the humanity within monstrous characters, a thematic concern that has defined his career.

The warning adds to growing debate within the entertainment industry about AI's role in creative work. Writers and actors struck last year in part over concerns about AI replacing human creativity, eventually securing contract language addressing the technology's use. Del Toro's comments suggest the conversation around AI and creative freedom remains unresolved, with fundamental questions about the nature of cinema itself now at stake.

The director's remarks highlight a critical moment for the film industry as it grapples with technological disruption. His call for vigilance against cinema illiteracy represents an appeal to preserve the visual literacy and creative craftsmanship that have defined cinema as an art form. As the industry continues to evolve, del Toro's voice joins others urging caution about the wholesale adoption of automation in creative fields where human judgment and artistic intention remain central to meaningful storytelling.

cards.headline: Universal Releases First Shrek 5 Trailer Featuring Adult Children
cards.teaser: The trailer for Shrek 5 shows the title characters and their grown children heading to jail alongside Donkey in the next installment of the franchise.
cards.body:
Universal unveiled the first trailer for Shrek 5 on Tuesday, giving fans an early look at the upcoming sequel. The trailer showcases Shrek, Fiona, Donkey, and the couple's now-adult children in a jail setting for their next adventure.

Mike Myers, Eddie Murphy, and Cameron Diaz reprise their roles voicing Shrek, Donkey, and Fiona respectively. The film is scheduled to release on June 30, 2027.

cards.headline: Disney Imagineering Adopts Adobe Firefly AI for Theme Park Design
cards.teaser: Disney's Imagineering Research Development unit is using Adobe's Firefly Foundry AI models to help design and visualize elements for upcoming theme parks.
cards.body:
Disney has turned to Adobe's AI technology months after a deal with OpenAI fell through. The company's Imagineering Research Development unit is now using Firefly Foundry, Adobe's commercial AI model, to assist in designing and visualizing components of Disney's future parks and attractions.

Firefly Foundry is the commercial version of Adobe's AI model, designed specifically to protect a brand's intellectual property. The tool allows Disney's Imagineers to work with AI-generated content while maintaining control over the company's creative assets and characters.

cards.headline: Sean Penn Developing Jan. 6 Police Officer Biopic Starring Bradley Cooper
cards.teaser: Director Sean Penn is planning a biographical film about a police officer involved in the January 6 Capitol events, with Bradley Cooper attached to star.
cards.body:
Sean Penn is set to write and direct a film about the January 6 Capitol riot, with Bradley Cooper starring in the lead role. Penn, who recently won his third Oscar, describes the project as a passion venture that will follow a police officer connected to the 2021 incident.

The film is being developed through Warner Bros., which has created complications as Paramount—a studio with close ties to former President Trump—pursues an acquisition of the studio.

cards.headline: Disclosure Day Takes Top Spot at UK and Ireland Box Office
cards.teaser: Universal's science fiction thriller Disclosure Day opened at number one in the UK and Ireland with an opening weekend of 5.5 million pounds.
cards.body:
Universal's sci-fi thriller Disclosure Day captured the top position at the UK and Ireland box office, earning 5.5 million pounds, equivalent to $7.3 million, in its opening weekend. The studio also secured the second-place slot with Curry Barker's horror-romance Obsession.

Obsession continued its strong performance in its fifth week of release, taking in $2 million and bringing its cumulative total higher. The film has emerged as a breakout title for Universal, maintaining momentum well beyond its initial release period.

cards.headline: Fox Nation Launches Stand-Up Comedy Specials With Jeff Foxworthy
cards.teaser: Fox Nation released Jeff Foxworthy's final stand-up comedy special as the streaming service expands into comedy programming.
cards.body:
Fox Nation has entered the stand-up comedy space with the release of Jeff Foxworthy's final comedy special. The streaming service, not traditionally known for comedy content, released the special earlier this month as part of a limited push into original comedy programming.

Fox Nation president Lauren Petterson distinguished the service's approach from competitors like Netflix, stating the platform is not pursuing a quantity-focused strategy. The streamer currently offers only a handful of original comedy specials, positioning itself as a specialty option rather than a volume player in the comedy streaming market.

cards.headline: Dolphin Entertainment and Kynetic Launch Graviteur Studios for Creator Economy
cards.teaser: Dolphin Entertainment and Kynetic Media Ventures have formed Graviteur Studios to produce modestly budgeted film and television projects aimed at the creator economy.
cards.body:
Dolphin Entertainment and Kynetic Media Ventures launched Graviteur Studios, a new production venture focused on tapping the creator economy for film and television projects. The studio will target productions with budgets ranging from $1 million to $10 million.

Dolphin CEO Bill O'Dowd and Kynetic CEO David Freeman are joining forces to lead the venture. The studio aims to work with creators on projects that bridge digital content creation and traditional entertainment production models.

hero.headline: Senate Republicans seek text of Iran agreement
hero.teaser: Senate Majority Leader John Thune says Republican leaders are pressing the Trump administration for the text of a memorandum of understanding with Iran but have not yet seen it.
hero.body:
Senate Majority Leader John Thune said Tuesday that Republican leaders are demanding to see the text of a memorandum of understanding that would end the military conflict with Iran, but have not yet received a briefing on the agreement.

"We're trying to get it," Thune told reporters at the Capitol, acknowledging that even senior lawmakers lack basic information about the preliminary accord announced Sunday.

The memorandum centers on reopening the Strait of Hormuz and lifting the United States' naval blockade in the region. It also includes potential financial incentives for Iran if the country meets certain conditions. Vice President JD Vance described the MOU as "a very general document" about a page long, with specifics to be determined during further negotiations.

Republican senators returning to Washington expressed widespread skepticism about the agreement. Thune said his primary concerns involve compliance and enforcement mechanisms. "I think the issues are going to be compliance, and how are you going to enforce that," he said, adding that the deal would be favorable if financial incentives are tied to Iran eliminating its enriched uranium and abandoning its nuclear program.

Senator Thom Tillis of North Carolina questioned the secrecy surrounding the agreement. "If it's a secret deal then how can I take it seriously?" he asked.

Other Republicans also sought clarity before the deal moves forward. The memorandum reportedly includes the possibility of releasing Iran's frozen funds, sanctions relief, and a 300 billion dollar reconstruction fund contingent on Tehran meeting specific benchmarks. Vance indicated that Gulf states would finance the reconstruction fund, not the United States.

Vance said the White House would release the text this week, emphasizing that "Iran doesn't get a dime of money unless they perform their obligations." However, the administration has not yet addressed key questions about verification of Iran's nuclear compliance or who will oversee the destruction of enriched uranium stored at damaged nuclear sites.

The agreement marks President Trump's second approach to Iran policy. He withdrew from the 2015 nuclear accord during his first term, a deal that allowed Iran to reclaim frozen assets. Trump has repeatedly criticized that agreement as sending "pallets of cash" to Iran.

Senator Lindsey Graham, a Trump ally and longtime Iran hawk, called for Congress to review and vote on the final agreement. "Let's look at it and see what it actually is," Graham said, expressing doubt about Iranian claims regarding the deal's benefits.

Vance responded by cautioning Graham and others against believing "hardliner propaganda in Iran" rather than focusing on the actual agreement terms.

cards.headline: FBI disrupts alleged plot targeting White House UFC event
cards.teaser: The FBI took multiple people into custody after disrupting an alleged threat against a UFC event held at the White House, FBI Director Kash Patel said Tuesday.
cards.body:
The FBI disrupted an alleged threat against a UFC event held at the White House over the weekend, FBI Director Kash Patel announced Tuesday. Multiple suspects are in custody. According to newly unsealed court documents, the plan involved using drones to target the event, which President Trump attended on his 80th birthday.

Law enforcement learned of the potential threat from people outside the Washington, D.C., area on June 10. Additional details about the suspects and charges are expected to be released as court documents are unsealed.

cards.headline: Trump dismisses Graham concerns over Iran deal
cards.teaser: President Trump brushed aside skepticism from Sen. Lindsey Graham over the preliminary agreement with Iran, saying the senator will be in big trouble.
cards.body:
President Trump responded to Sen. Lindsey Graham's skepticism about a preliminary Iran agreement while attending the G7 summit in France. When asked by reporters about Graham's concerns, Trump said he would need to speak with the South Carolina senator, characterizing him as "good and fine" and asserting that Graham is not actually skeptical of the deal.

Trump has promoted the agreement as successful and indicated that upcoming negotiations will proceed more smoothly than the initial talks. French President Emmanuel Macron met with Trump at the summit and congratulated him on reaching the Iran accord.

cards.headline: Pence says Trump deserves latitude on Iran agreement
cards.teaser: Former Vice President Mike Pence said President Trump deserves latitude on reaching a preliminary agreement with Iran, while noting he has very real concerns.
cards.body:
Rewritten Card

Former Vice President Mike Pence said President Trump deserves flexibility in negotiating a preliminary agreement with Iran. Pence pointed to Trump's past military actions against Iran as justification for giving the president room to maneuver in talks.

However, Pence expressed reservations about the deal itself, saying he maintains "very real concerns" about its terms. His measured stance reflects a broader Republican approach of supporting Trump while remaining cautious about the specifics of any Iran agreement.

cards.headline: Schiff calls Justice Department investigation of Newsom deliberate
cards.teaser: Sen. Adam Schiff said a reported Justice Department investigation into California Gov. Gavin Newsom is not coincidental, calling it deliberate.
cards.body:
Sen. Adam Schiff said a reported Department of Justice investigation into California Gov. Gavin Newsom is deliberate rather than coincidental. The California Democrat said the decision to investigate a likely Democratic presidential candidate and his family was not purely random.

Schiff's comments suggest he views the investigation as politically motivated. Newsom is considered a potential Democratic candidate for president, and the reported Justice Department probe involves both the governor and his family.

cards.headline: Trump says Russia should make peace deal with Ukraine
cards.teaser: President Trump said Russia should make a deal with Ukraine to end the four-year invasion, noting both countries have lost tremendous numbers of people.
cards.body:
At the Group of Seven summit in France, President Trump urged Russia to negotiate an end to its four-year invasion of Ukraine. Trump emphasized that both Russia and Ukraine have suffered significant losses in the conflict.

Trump's remarks came as G7 allies worked to keep Ukraine on the agenda amid discussions about Middle East tensions. The president has previously expressed interest in negotiating a resolution to the war.

cards.headline: Trump touts Iran deal at G7 summit
cards.teaser: President Trump said the deal with Iran is done and should be successful, adding that a second stage of negotiations will be easier.
cards.body:
President Trump announced a completed agreement with Iran while attending the G7 Summit in France. French President Emmanuel Macron congratulated Trump on signing the new Iran deal. Trump expressed confidence that the agreement should be successful and suggested future negotiations will be easier.

During the summit, Trump also urged Israel to reduce its military operations against Lebanon. G7 leaders used the gathering to discuss ongoing conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine, with Trump framing the Iran agreement as a major diplomatic achievement.
